label: S. 5326

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act amends the Social Security Act to provide increased and ongoing funding for federal health care fraud and abuse control programs from fiscal year 2027 onward. It expands investigative authority for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Office of the Inspector General, clarifies definitions regarding public and private health plans, incorporates the Children's Health Insurance Program into data-matching initiatives, alters annual reporting deadlines with required notices for delays, and mandates a Government Accountability Office (GAO) study and report on program performance.

affected_groups.effect: Receive increased funding appropriations for fiscal years 2027 through 2029 and onward, with explicit authority to detect or prosecute fraud and communicate with the public.
Included in the Medicare-Medicaid Data Match Program beginning in 2027.

key_provisions: Provides specific funding increases for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029 (with consumer price index adjustments thereafter) for HHS, the HHS Office of the Inspector General, the FBI, the Medicare Integrity Program, and the Medicare-Medicaid Data Match Program.
Expands the investigative authority of the HHS Office of the Inspector General to include certain programs established under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.
Clarifies definitions of health plans to include both public and private delivery, plans, and programs.
Extends the Medicare-Medicaid Data Match Program to include the State Children's Health Insurance Program beginning in 2027.
Changes the annual reporting deadline for the Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control report to April 1 and requires joint notices of delay to specified congressional committees if the report is late.
Requires the Comptroller General to conduct a study and report to Congress within 16 months regarding the performance and effectiveness of the Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program.

It expands investigative authority for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Office of the Inspector General, clarifies definitions regarding public and private health plans, incorporates the Children's Health Insurance Program into data-matching initiatives, alters annual reporting deadlines with required notices for delays, and mandates a Government Accountability Office (GAO) study and report on program performance.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal funding streams and oversight structures for health care fraud enforcement across multiple agencies. Because the source text contains no information on broader macroeconomic impacts, overall budget context, or likelihood of passage, its significance is strictly measured by the statutory modifications made to federal fraud oversight programs and their multi-million dollar funding increases.
